The '''1948-49 Serie A''' was the forty-seventh edition of the [[Italian Football Championship]]. It was the sixteenth Italian Football Championship [[brand]]ed [[Serie A]], since Serie A was launched in [[1929–30 Serie A|1929]]. This was the twenty-third season from which the Italian Football Champions adorned their team jerseys in the subsequent season with a [[Scudetto]].

At the request of rival teams [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] were declared champions on 6 May 1949, two days after the [[Superga air disaster]] killed their entire first team squad.<ref name=BBC>{{cite web |author=Patrick Jennings |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/46788983 |title=The plane crash that killed Serie A's champions and their English coach |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 January 2019 }}</ref> At the time of the declaration, Torino led the runner-up Internazionale by four points with four matches remaining.<ref name=rsssf>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070808041922/http://www.rsssf.com/tablesi/ital49.html] - All results on [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF]] Website.></ref> Torino's remaining four matches were played by their [[reserve team]], finishing the league five points ahead of the runner up. Torino were thus champions for the sixth time in their [[history]]. This was their sixth scudetto since the scudetto started being awarded in [[1923–24 Prima Divisione|1924]] and their fourth win contested as Serie A. This was their last of five consecutive Italian Football Championship wins, punctuated by a two-year break due to [[World War II]].

==Teams==
[[Novara Calcio|Novara]] for Northern Italy, [[Padova Calcio|Padova]] for Central Italy and [[US Palermo|Palermo]] for Southern Italy had been promoted from [[Serie B]].

==Events==
Following the restoration of ordinary Serie B championship, the [[FIGC]] decided to come back to two relegations only from Serie A.
